Command: Do not profane God's holy name
Summary: One of the two sides of Leviticus 22:32: do not profane God's holy name. God's name is hallowed by his people's conduct, and profaned by it.
Commandment: Do not profane God's holy name
Application: Scripture's stated reason: I am the LORD which hallow you, that brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God (Leviticus 22:32-33).
Purpose: Scripture's stated reason: I am the LORD which hallow you, that brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God (Leviticus 22:32-33).
Function: Moral law, plain and simple: it binds wherever people live, in any age. One of the two sides of Leviticus 22:32: do not profane God's holy name. Scripture gives the reason: I am the LORD which hallow you, that brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God. The restraint is the prohibition itself: do not profane God's holy name.
